newsitem.title: USA: Dow Chemical found negligent in implant trial.
newsitem.headline: Dow Chemical found negligent in implant trial.

text.p: Women suing the Dow Chemical Co. for its role in testing silicone breast implants won a major victory on Monday as a jury ruled the company was negligent and intentionally withheld information about implant dangers.

The state district court jury here, ruling in the first phase of a landmark class action suit, found that Dow Chemical was negligent in testing silicone for use in human implants, intentionally withheld information, knowingly made misleading statements about their safety and conspired with manufacturer Dow Corning Inc.
Dow Corning is a 50-50 joint venture of Dow Chemical and Corning Inc.
About 30 women who were part of the lawsuit wept openly and hugged each other as the verdict was read.
"This validates what we've been saying all along. We had a product put in our bodies that was not safe," Connie Hebert of Avondale, La., said.
"We need to be accepted by the medical community so they can start finding cures for our illnesses instead of sending us to psychiatrists for anti-depressants," said Nikki Kaufman of Algiers, La.
The jury deliberated less than two days following five months of trial testimony and courtroom skirmishes as Dow Chemical attorneys tried to have the trial stopped or transferred out of state.
The trial marks the first time that a class-action suit has been brought by women who underwent the controversial proceedure. Previous cases have dealt with individuals.
Eight women, representing 10,000 breast implant recipients, brought the suit.
The second phase of the trial, in which the same jury will determine if silicone breast implants actually made recipients ill, will begin Sept. 29, attorneys said.

"This shows an American jury can't be fooled," lead counsel for the women, John O'Quinn, said after the verdict was read. "Three out of three times, juries have evaluated all the evidence and found the giant chemical company guilty."
Juries awarded damages to individual plaintiffs in Nevada and Texas, he said.
Thousands of women who received breast implants, 80 percent of which were for cosmetic purposes, claim to have suffered autoimmune and connective disorders as a result of the silicone implants.
Dow Chemical's lead attorney, Lorna Propes, said after the verdict that the company was disappointed. "We believe we're absolutely right and that science and the facts are on our side," she said.
"Dow Chemical did not manufacture breast implants. Breast implants do not cause harm," Propes said.

Propes said her understanding is that Dow Chemical cannot appeal until the entire four-part trial process ends. But she added that the company intended to appeal, especially if it lost the second phase.
Dow Chemical stock was off $2 at $90 a share on the New York Stock Exchange after the verdict, but analysts said it was too early to determine the potential long-term impact of the ruling.
"In many cases a jury will find for a group of lawyers that they happpen to like, and it has nothing to do with logic," Oppenheimer & Co. analyst Jeffrey Spetalnick said.

State District Court Judge Yada MaGee at one point declared a mistrial based on two plaintiff's attorneys having established too great a rapport with the jury but reversed the ruling after polling jurors.
Corning Inc.'s stock fell $1.56 to $61.50 on the NYSE.
